verses.original: And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and brought forth Cain and said, I have gained a man through God.

verses.lyric:
Again she bore, his brother Abel.
Abel kept the sheep,
while Cain worked the ground.
verses.original: And she again bore his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

verses.lyric:
After a time Cain brought
fruit of the earth
as an offering to the Lord.
verses.original: And it was so after some time that Cain brought of the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to the Lord.

verses.lyric:
Abel brought the firstborn of his sheep,
and his fatlings.
God looked upon Abel and his gifts.
verses.original: And Abel also brought of the firstborn of his sheep and of his fatlings, and God looked upon Abel and his gifts,

verses.lyric:
But Cain and his sacrifices
He did not regard.
Cain was deeply grieved;
his face fell low.
verses.original: but Cain and his sacrifices he regarded not, and Cain was exceedingly sorrowful and his countenance fell.

verses.lyric:
The Lord God asked Cain,
Why are you so sorrowful?
Why has your face fallen?
verses.original: And the Lord God said to Cain, Why art thou become very sorrowful and why is thy countenance fallen?

verses.lyric:
If you brought it rightly
but did not divide it rightly,
have you not sinned?
Be still; he shall submit to you,
and you shall rule over him.
verses.original: Hast thou not sinned if thou hast brought it rightly, but not rightly divided it? be still, to thee shall be his submission, and thou shalt rule over him.

verses.lyric:
Cain said to Abel his brother,
Let us go out to the plain.
There in the plain he rose against Abel
and killed his brother.
verses.original: And Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go out into the plain; and it came to pass that when they were in the plain Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

verses.lyric:
The Lord God asked Cain,
Where is Abel, your brother?
I do not know, he said;
am I my brother's keeper?
verses.original: And the Lord God said to Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? and he said, I know not, am I my brother's keeper?
And the Lord said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood cries to me out of the ground.

verses.lyric:
Now you are cursed from the earth;
she opened her mouth
to take your brother's blood
from your hand.
verses.original: And now thou [art] cursed from the earth which has opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.

verses.lyric:
When you till the earth,
she will no longer yield her strength.
You will groan and tremble
upon the earth.
verses.original: When thou tillest the earth, then it shall not continue to give its strength to thee: thou shalt be groaning and trembling on the earth.

verses.lyric:
Cain said to the Lord God,
My crime is too great
for me to be forgiven.
verses.original: And Cain said to the Lord God, My crime [is] too great for me to be forgiven.

verses.lyric:
If You cast me out today
from the face of the earth,
hidden from Your presence,
groaning and trembling on the earth,
whoever finds me will kill me.
verses.original: If thou castest me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy presence, and I shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth, then it will be that any one that finds me shall slay me.

verses.lyric:
The Lord God said, Not so.
Whoever kills Cain
will suffer vengeance sevenfold.
The Lord set a mark upon Cain,
so none who found him would kill him.
verses.original: And the Lord God said to him, Not so, any one that slays Cain shall suffer seven-fold vengeance; and the Lord God set a mark upon Cain that no one that found him might slay him.

verses.lyric:
Cain went out from God's presence
and lived in the land of Nod,
across from Edem.
verses.original: So Cain went forth from the presence of God and dwelt in the land of Nod over against Edem.

verses.lyric:
Cain knew his wife;
she conceived and bore Enoch.
He built a city
and named it for his son, Enoch.
verses.original: And Cain knew his wife, and having conceived she bore Enoch; and he built a city; and he named the city after the name of his son, Enoch.

verses.lyric:
To Enoch was born Gaidad.
Gaidad fathered Maleleel,
Maleleel fathered Mathusala,
and Mathusala fathered Lamech.
verses.original: And to Enoch was born Gaidad; and Gaidad begot Maleleel; and Maleleel begot Mathusala; and Mathusala begot Lamech.

verses.lyric:
Lamech took two wives: 
one was named Ada,
the other Sella.
verses.original: And Lamech took to himself two wives; the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the second Sella.

verses.lyric:
Ada bore Jobel,
father of those who live in tents
and tend the cattle.
verses.original: And Ada bore Jobel; he was the father of those that dwell in tents, feeding cattle.
And the name of his brother was Jubal; he it was who invented the psaltery and harp.

verses.lyric:
Sella bore Thobel,
a smith of brass and iron.
Thobel's sister was Noëma.
verses.original: And Sella also bore Thobel; he was a smith, a manufacturer both of brass and iron; and the sister of Thobel was Noëma.

verses.lyric:
Lamech said to Ada and Sella,
Hear my voice, wives of Lamech;
listen to my words.
I have killed a man to my sorrow,
a young man to my grief.
verses.original: And Lamech said to his wives, Ada and Sella, Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech, consider my words, because I have slain a man to my sorrow and a youth to my grief.

verses.lyric:
Because vengeance was taken seven times for Cain,
for Lamech it will be
seventy times seven.
verses.original: Because vengeance has been exacted seven times on Cain's behalf, on Lamech's [it shall be] seventy times seven.

verses.lyric:
Adam knew Eve his wife again.
She bore a son and named him Seth: 
God has raised another seed for me
in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.
verses.original: And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Seth, saying, For God has raised up to me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.

verses.lyric:
Seth also had a son
and named him Enos.
He hoped to call upon
the name of the Lord God.
verses.original: And Seth had a son, and he called his name Enos: he hoped to call on the name of the Lord God.

scriptureSource: Modern Septuagint song adaptation; original verse text: Brenton Septuagint
